## Abstract

Survey-based research relies on the assumption that respondents adequately
represent the population of interest. However, differential nonresponse can
introduce substantial bias.

Using data from a university campus climate survey, we compare respondent
characteristics with known population characteristics and investigate
post-stratification weighting as one method for reducing observed
imbalances.

Our analysis illustrates why response rate alone is an incomplete measure
of survey quality and highlights the importance of examining who is
represented in collected data.

**Keywords:** survey sampling, nonresponse, weighting, missing data
